topicName: Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, and Apache Hudi internals
content:
[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Deep Dive into Modern Lakehouse Formats: Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, and Apache Hudi Internals"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"The rise of the data lakehouse architecture bridges the gap between traditional data warehouses and low-cost cloud object storage. At the heart of this paradigm shift are open table formats: Apache Iceberg, Delta Lake, and Apache Hudi. This tutorial explores the architectural internals of these three formats, focusing on how they manage metadata, concurrency control, and file layouts."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. Architectural Overview and Metadata Design"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"Traditional data lakes suffered from file listing performance issues and lack of ACID transactions. Open table formats solve this by introducing a metadata layer that sits between the physical data files (Parquet, ORC, Avro) and the query engines (Spark, Trino, Flink)."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apache Iceberg: Uses a hierarchical metadata tree consisting of catalog, metadata file, manifest list, and manifest files, ensuring independence from physical directory structures."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Delta Lake: Relies on an _delta_log directory containing JSON transaction log files and checkpoint Parquet files, mirroring a sequential log-structured file system."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Apache Hudi: Organizes data into a timeline using commit, clean, and compaction actions, storing metadata in a .hoodie timeline directory alongside timeline metadata files."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Apache Iceberg Internals"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"Iceberg was designed from the ground up to handle massive tables without directory listing bottlenecks. Its metadata model allows engines to prune files using column-level statistics (min/max values, null counts) stored directly in manifest files."},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"Iceberg Metadata Hierarchy:
Catalog -> v1.metadata.json -> snapshot-list -> manifest-list (.avro) -> manifest-file (.avro) -> data files (.parquet)"},{"order":11,"type":"paragraph","text":"Iceberg supports hidden partitioning, meaning users do not need to include partition columns explicitly in queries. The format manages the transformation from raw data values to partition values automatically within the manifest layer."},{"order":12,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Delta Lake Internals"},{"order":13,"type":"paragraph","text":"Delta Lake, built on top of Apache Spark, manages tables via transactional logs. Every write operation generates a new JSON file (e.g., 000000.json) containing actions like addFile, removeFile, and metadata updates."},{"order":14,"type":"code","text":"Delta Log Structure Example:
{"add": {"path": "part-0.parquet", "size": 832, "partitionValues": {}, "dataChange": true}}
{"commitInfo": {"operation": "WRITE", "readVersion": 0}}"},{"order":15,"type":"paragraph","text":"To prevent log reading bottlenecks during planning, Delta Lake periodically compacts JSON logs into Parquet checkpoint files. Concurrency is handled using Optimistic Concurrency Control (OCC) with mutual exclusion on cloud storage."},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"4. Apache Hudi Internals"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Apache Hudi (Hadoop Upserts Deletes and Incrementals) is specifically optimized for stream ingestion and row-level mutations. Hudi introduces two storage types: Copy-on-Write (CoW) and Merge-on-Read (MoR)."},{"order":18,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Copy-on-Write (CoW): Updates rewrite entire Parquet files, making writes slightly heavier but reads optimal."},{"order":19,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Merge-on-Read (MoR): Writes updates to fast delta logs (Avro) and merges them with base Parquet files during compaction or read time, minimizing write latency."},{"order":20,"type":"subheading","text":"5. Comparative Summary for Data Architects"},{"order":21,"type":"paragraph","text":"Choosing the right format depends on your enterprise requirements. Iceberg excels in multi-engine flexibility (Spark, Trino, Flink, Presto) and hidden partitioning. Delta Lake offers tight integration with the Spark ecosystem and robust transaction management. Hudi is unmatched for high-frequency row-level updates and incremental processing pipelines."}]
